examples.en: When meditating, I sit in the lotus position.
I sat cross-legged for a long time and now my legs are numb.

examples.ko: 스님이 가부좌를 튼 채 눈을 감고 계세요.
examples.en: The monk is sitting in the lotus position with his eyes closed.
I learned the lotus pose in yoga class.
The lotus position is uncomfortable for me, so I sat on a chair.
Don't sit in the lotus position. Sit comfortably.

explain: '가부좌를 틀다'가 가장 흔한 짝이에요. 발을 반대쪽 허벅지 위에 올려 앉는 자세를 가리키고, 편하게 다리를 꼬아 앉는 '양반다리'와는 달라요. 명상, 요가, 불교 이야기에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: The most common pairing is '가부좌를 틀다'. It refers to sitting with the feet placed on the opposite thighs, which is different from '양반다리', the casual cross-legged sit. You often hear it in talk about meditation, yoga and Buddhism.

examples.en: This house has a very sturdy main beam.
The main beam of an old hanok is thick and looks impressive.
He is a reliable pillar of our company.

examples.ko: 젊은 선수들이 팀의 대들보로 자라고 있어요.
examples.en: The young players are growing into the backbone of the team.
We took a family photo under the main beam.

examples.ko: 아버지는 우리 집안의 대들보 같은 분이세요.
examples.en: My father is like the pillar of our family.

explain: 집을 지을 때 지붕을 받치는 중요한 가로 나무를 말하고, 그래서 집안·회사·나라를 이끄는 중심 인물을 비유할 때도 써요. 비슷한 말로 '기둥'이 있어요. 사람에게 쓰면 믿고 기대는 사람이라는 칭찬이에요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 집안을 책임지고 이끄는 중심인물을 가리켜요. 회사나 나라에도 '회사의 대들보', '나라의 대들보'처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to the key person who carries and leads the family. It is also used as 'a pillar of the company' or 'a pillar of the nation'.

explain_en: It is the main horizontal beam that supports a roof, and by extension it describes the central figure of a family, company, or country. A similar word is '기둥'. Said about a person, it is praise for someone people rely on.

examples.en: In winter, cranes fly to Cheorwon.
A crane rests standing on one leg.

examples.ko: 하얀 두루미 한 쌍이 논에 내려앉았어요.
examples.en: A pair of white cranes landed in the rice field.

examples.ko: 그림 속 두루미가 날개를 활짝 폈어요.
examples.en: The crane in the painting spread its wings wide.

examples.ko: 두루미는 오래 사는 새로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: The crane is known as a long-lived bird.
The photographer went out at dawn to photograph cranes.

explain: 다리와 목이 긴 흰 새로, 오래 살고 품위 있는 새로 여겨요. 한국에서는 '학'이라고도 하는데, 옛 그림이나 이야기에서는 '학'이 더 자주 나와요. 겨울 철새라서 겨울에 만날 수 있어요.
explain_en: A white bird with long legs and neck, seen as long-lived and dignified. In Korea it is also called 학, and old paintings and tales use 학 more often. It is a winter migrant, so you can meet it in winter.

examples.ko: 저는 냄새에 둔감해서 잘 못 맡아요.
examples.en: I'm not sensitive to smells, so I can't smell well.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 남의 기분에 너무 둔감해요.
examples.en: He is too insensitive to other people's feelings.

examples.ko: 추위에 둔감한 편이라 겨울에도 얇게 입어요.
examples.en: I don't really feel the cold, so I dress lightly even in winter.

examples.ko: 변화에 둔감하면 일하기 힘들어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you're slow to notice change, work can become hard.
They say you become less sensitive to taste as you get older.
I don't know why I was so oblivious to the mood.

explain: 반대말은 '민감하다'이고, 보통 '~에 둔감하다'처럼 '에'와 같이 써요. 말할 때는 '눈치가 없다', '무디다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '민감하다', and it is usually used as '~에 둔감하다' with the particle '에'. In speech people also say '눈치가 없다' or '무디다'.

examples.en: That movie was really romantic.
A candlelit dinner is romantic.
My boyfriend wrote me a romantic letter.
He is someone who expresses love romantically.
We are not a romantic couple.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날은 로맨틱해서 걷고 싶어요.
examples.en: Rainy days feel romantic, so I want to go for a walk.

explain: '로맨틱하다'는 사랑하는 사이의 분위기, 사람, 장소를 말할 때 써요. 같은 뜻의 '낭만적이다'는 조금 더 글 같고, 사랑이 아니어도 여행이나 꿈처럼 낭만이 있는 것에 써요. 영화 장르 '로맨틱 코미디'는 줄여서 '로코'라고 해요.
explain_en: 로맨틱하다 describes the mood of a loving couple, a person, or a place. The similar 낭만적이다 sounds a bit more literary and also fits non-love things such as travel or dreams. The film genre 'romantic comedy' is shortened to 로코.

en: palatable; agreeable to the taste; pleasant-tasting

examples.ko: 할머니가 만든 김치는 색도 곱고 맛깔스러워요.
examples.en: The kimchi my grandmother made has a lovely color and looks delicious.

examples.ko: 맛깔스러운 반찬이 식탁에 가득해서 배가 더 고파졌어요.
examples.en: The table was full of appetizing side dishes, and I got even hungrier.

examples.ko: 사진 속 음식이 정말 맛깔스러워 보여요.
examples.en: The food in the photo looks really appetizing.

examples.ko: 그분은 이야기를 맛깔스럽게 풀어 줘서 듣는 재미가 있어요.
examples.en: She tells stories so vividly that they are fun to listen to.

examples.ko: 빛깔이 맛깔스럽고 향도 좋아서 한 입 먹어 봤어요.
examples.en: The color looked tasty and the smell was good, so I tried a bite.

examples.ko: 그날 먹은 비빔밥은 맛깔스러웠던 기억으로 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The bibimbap I ate that day remains a delicious memory.

explain: 음식이 보기에도 먹음직하고 맛있어 보일 때 써요. 말솜씨나 글이 감칠맛 나게 재미있을 때도 '맛깔스럽게 말하다'처럼 쓸 수 있어요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '맛깔스러워요', '맛깔스러운'이 되고, '맛있다'보다 글 같은 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used when food looks as appetizing as it tastes. It can also describe skillful, flavorful speech or writing, as in '맛깔스럽게 말하다'. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '맛깔스러워요' and '맛깔스러운', and it sounds more literary than '맛있다'.

examples.en: Last night's game was a real classic.

examples.ko: 두 팀이 연장전까지 가는 명승부를 펼쳤어요.
examples.en: The two teams put on a great game that went into extra time.

examples.ko: 이번 결승전은 오랫동안 명승부로 기억될 거예요.
examples.en: This final will be remembered as a great game for a long time.

examples.ko: 명승부 끝에 우리 팀이 아쉽게 졌어요.
examples.en: After a great game, our team narrowly lost.

examples.ko: 친구랑 옛날 명승부 영상을 다시 봤어요.
examples.en: I rewatched a video of an old classic game with my friend.

examples.ko: 팬들은 그 경기를 올림픽 최고의 명승부라고 말해요.
examples.en: Fans call that match the best game in Olympic history.

explain: 경기가 끝까지 팽팽하고 재미있었을 때 쓰는 말이라서 스포츠 기사나 해설에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '진짜 재밌는 경기였어요'라고 해도 되지만, 오래 기억에 남는 경기에는 '명승부'가 잘 어울려요. 보통 '명승부를 펼치다', '명승부가 되다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a match stayed tight and exciting until the end, so it often appears in sports articles and commentary. In daily talk you can just say '진짜 재밌는 경기였어요', but '명승부' fits a game people will remember. It is usually used as '명승부를 펼치다' or '명승부가 되다'.

examples.en: Coming out into the outside world after a long time, the light was dazzling.
The child was curious about the outside world and just looked out the window.
I was only in the hospital, so I didn't know the news from outside.
Studying abroad showed me the wider world.
The outside world is bigger than you think.

examples.ko: 바깥세상과 연락이 끊긴 채 일주일을 지냈어요.
examples.en: I spent a week cut off from the outside world.

explain: 지금 내가 있는 집, 학교, 병원 같은 좁은 곳 밖의 넓은 세상을 말해요. 갇혀 있거나 오래 쉬다가 나왔을 때, 또는 경험이 좁았던 사람이 시야를 넓힐 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means the wide world beyond a small place such as your home, school or hospital. It is often used when someone comes out after being shut in or resting a long time, or when someone with limited experience widens their view.

examples.en: Grandmother took a needle out of the sewing box.
A button fell off, so I looked for the sewing box.

examples.ko: 반짇고리 안에는 실과 가위가 들어 있어요.
examples.en: There are thread and scissors in the sewing box.

examples.ko: 반짇고리는 서랍장 맨 아래 칸에 있어요.
examples.en: The sewing box is in the bottom drawer of the chest.
I didn't have a sewing box, so I borrowed a needle from a neighbor.
My mom's old sewing box is full of memories.

explain: 바늘, 실, 가위, 단추 같은 바느질 도구를 담아 두는 그릇이에요. 요즘 여행용 작은 세트는 '바느질 세트'라고도 해요. 'ㄷ' 받침이 있어서 쓸 때 '반짇고리'로 써야 하는 점을 주의하세요.
explain_en: It is a container that holds sewing tools such as needles, thread, scissors and buttons. A small travel set is nowadays also called a '바느질 세트' (sewing set). Watch the spelling: it is written with the 'ㄷ' batchim as '반짇고리'.

examples.en: It looks plain on the outside, but the inside is very clean.
That shop is in a shabby-looking building.
At first the room looked really unimpressive.
The gift looks so plain that I'm a little embarrassed.
After changing clothes, my shabby look was transformed.

examples.ko: 이 의자는 볼품없게 생겼지만 앉기 편해요.
examples.en: This chair looks plain, but it's comfortable to sit in.

explain: 겉모양이 초라하거나 보잘것없을 때 써요. '초라하다'는 처지나 형편에도 쓰지만, '볼품없다'는 모양새에 더 집중해요. 한 단어라 붙여 쓰고, 반대는 '볼품 있다'예요.
explain_en: It is used when something looks shabby or unimpressive. '초라하다' can also describe one's situation, while '볼품없다' focuses on appearance. It is written as one word, and the opposite is '볼품 있다'.

examples.en: When I asked, my friend helped me without hesitation.

examples.ko: 사장님이 휴가 신청을 선선히 허락해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My boss readily approved my vacation request.
He readily admitted his own mistake.

examples.ko: 값을 깎아 달라고 하자 주인이 선선히 깎아 줬어요.
examples.en: When I asked for a discount, the owner gave one without fuss.
My father accepted my decision without any fuss.
I didn't expect them to agree so readily.

explain: 망설이거나 따지지 않고 시원스럽게 허락하고 받아들이는 태도를 말해요. '허락하다', '인정하다', '도와주다' 같은 말과 자주 쓰고, 비슷한 말로 '흔쾌히'가 있어요.
explain_en: It describes agreeing or accepting in a free and easy way, without hesitating or arguing. It often goes with verbs like '허락하다' (permit), '인정하다' (admit) and '도와주다' (help), and a similar word is '흔쾌히' (gladly).

examples.en: My friend is a famous classical singer.
The classical singer sang the opera song beautifully.

examples.ko: 저는 어렸을 때 성악가가 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I wanted to become a classical singer.

examples.ko: 성악가는 마이크 없이도 목소리가 크게 들려요.
examples.en: A classical singer's voice is heard loudly even without a microphone.
World-famous classical singers are coming to today's concert.
I took a photo with the classical singer.

explain: 성악가는 오페라나 클래식 노래를 부르는 가수를 말해서 대중가요 가수는 '가수'라고 해요. 마이크 없이 소리를 멀리 보내는 발성을 배운 사람이라는 느낌이 있어요. 악기를 연주하면 '연주가'나 '피아니스트'처럼 달라져요.
explain_en: 성악가 is a singer of opera or classical songs, while pop singers are simply '가수'. It suggests someone trained to project their voice far without a microphone. Instrument players are called '연주가' or names like '피아니스트'.

en: be revised; be corrected; be edited

examples.en: The report was revised, so I sent it again.
If the schedule is changed, I'll tell you right away.

examples.ko: 틀린 부분이 모두 수정되었는지 확인해 주세요.
examples.en: Please check whether all the wrong parts have been corrected.

examples.ko: 계획이 여러 번 수정된 끝에 완성됐어요.
examples.en: The plan was finished after being revised several times.
Leave the files that haven't been edited as they are.
The error will be fixed in the next update.

explain: 글·문서·계획·프로그램의 내용이 고쳐질 때 써요. 사람이 고치면 '수정하다', 내용이 주어이면 '수정되다'예요. 같은 소리의 '수정'에는 보석 '수정'도 있어서 문장을 보고 구분해요.
explain_en: Use it when the content of a text, document, plan, or program gets changed. When a person does the fixing it is '수정하다'; when the content is the subject it is '수정되다'. There is also '수정' meaning crystal, so rely on the sentence to tell them apart.

examples.en: I put an armchair in the living room.
I sat in an armchair and read a book.
This armchair is really comfortable.
The armchair was so soft that I fell asleep.
My father sits in the armchair and watches the news.
I went to a furniture store to buy an armchair.

explain: 등받이와 팔걸이가 있고 푹신해서 편하게 앉는 의자를 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '편한 의자'나 '소파'라고 말하는 경우도 많아요. 가구점 설명이나 글에서 더 자주 보이는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a soft chair with a back and armrests that you can relax in. In daily conversation people often say '편한 의자' or '소파' instead. The word shows up more in furniture descriptions and writing.

examples.ko: 산 정상에서 내려다본 풍경은 정말 절경이었어요.
examples.en: The view from the top of the mountain was truly spectacular.

examples.ko: 제주도에는 바다 절경을 볼 수 있는 곳이 많아요.
examples.en: Jeju Island has many places with spectacular sea views.
Seoraksan in autumn colors is famous for its breathtaking scenery.

examples.ko: 그 절경을 보려고 새벽에 일어나서 올라갔어요.
examples.en: I got up at dawn and climbed up to see that breathtaking view.

examples.ko: 이 카페는 창밖으로 보이는 절경 덕분에 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This cafe is popular thanks to the spectacular view outside its windows.

examples.ko: 눈 덮인 산이 만드는 절경에 모두 말을 잃었어요.
examples.en: Everyone was speechless at the stunning scenery of the snow-covered mountains.

explain: '경치가 좋다'보다 훨씬 강하게 감탄할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 주로 산·바다·계곡 같은 자연 풍경에 쓰고, 도시의 밤 풍경에는 '멋진 야경'처럼 다른 말을 많이 써요. '절경이다', '절경을 이루다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It expresses much stronger admiration than '경치가 좋다'. It is mainly for natural views like mountains, the sea and valleys; for a city at night people usually say '멋진 야경' instead. You can say '절경이다' or '절경을 이루다'.

examples.ko: 옛날 사람들은 산 위에 성을 축조했어요.
examples.en: People in the old days built a fortress on top of the mountain.

examples.ko: 이 다리는 백 년 전에 축조한 거예요.
examples.en: This bridge was built a hundred years ago.

examples.ko: 둑을 축조하는 데 오랜 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a long time to build the embankment.

examples.ko: 튼튼하게 축조해야 홍수에도 견딜 수 있어요.
examples.en: It has to be built solidly to withstand floods.
The government decided to build a new harbor.
It was constructed by stacking bricks, but it collapsed soon.

explain: '짓다'보다 딱딱한 말로, 성, 둑, 다리처럼 쌓아서 만드는 큰 구조물에 어울려요. 집이나 건물은 일상에서 '짓다'를 쓰고, 축조는 설명문이나 역사 이야기에서 주로 나와요. 피동은 '축조되다'예요.
explain_en: It is a stiffer word than '짓다', suited to large structures built up by stacking, such as fortresses, embankments and bridges. For houses and buildings people say '짓다' in daily life, and '축조' mostly appears in explanatory texts and history. The passive form is '축조되다'.

examples.ko: 오늘 사회 시간에 풀뿌리 민주주의를 배웠어요.
examples.en: Today in social studies we learned about grassroots democracy.
They say that in the old days, people were so poor they ate grass roots.
I had a hard time pulling grass roots in the garden.
A grassroots group helps with the village cleanup.

examples.ko: 잡초는 풀뿌리까지 뽑아야 다시 안 나요.
examples.en: Weeds won't come back unless you pull them out by the roots.
A grassroots citizens' movement changed the policy.

explain: 풀의 뿌리라는 뜻으로도 쓰지만 뉴스에서는 '일반 시민이 중심이 되는'이라는 뜻으로 더 자주 나와요. '풀뿌리 민주주의', '풀뿌리 단체'처럼 뒤에 명사가 붙어요.

phrases.example: 지역 주민이 직접 참여하는 것이 풀뿌리 민주주의의 시작이에요.
phrases.en: Residents taking part directly is the start of grassroots democracy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주민과 시민이 직접 참여해 만드는 민주주의를 말해요. 뉴스와 수업에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to democracy built by residents and citizens taking part directly. It often appears in news and classes.

explain_en: It can mean the roots of grass, but in the news it more often means 'led by ordinary citizens'. It usually comes before a noun, as in '풀뿌리 민주주의' and '풀뿌리 단체'.
